## reference · service-hailing-grab-matching-factors
* Grab's allocation algorithms have two main objectives: meeting everyone's needs and ensuring fairness for all partners.
* The algorithms do not unfairly discriminate based on demographic characteristics, except in cases where safety or cultural/religious sensitivities are a concern.
* Grab prioritizes allocation to partners who enable auto-acceptance of requests to reduce cherry-picking and increase efficiency.
* The algorithms match requests with partners based on factors such as:
	+ Vehicle type and size
	+ Partner training and experience
	+ Familiarity with navigation and city roads
* Grab strives to ensure all partners have adequate earnings, while rewarding higher-performers through schemes like priority allocation.
* Safety is never compromised, and partners are free to take breaks and resume work at their discretion.
* In scenarios with insufficient partners, the algorithm prioritizes fulfilling as many consumer requests as possible, such as by grouping nearby orders together.
* In scenarios with insufficient requests, the algorithm decides which partner to allocate the request to based on principles like fairness, efficiency, and partner preferences.
Sources: https://www.grab.com/sg/blog/public-policy/how-does-grab-match-trips-and-orders-to-driver-and-delivery-partners/
